name: Damask
author: Erin Carter
description: A brocade wallpaper of mirror-symmetric foliate medallions on a half-drop repeat. Each cell folds a noise field through an N-fold dihedral kaleidoscope into an ornate, perfectly symmetric motif; the deep jewel ground carries the pattern tone-on-tone like real damask while gold filigree outlines the ornament. Lit evenly across the whole frame, no dark midriff.

params.label: Motif size
params.effect: Size of each repeating medallion in CSS pixels - a dense small-figured brocade at the minimum, a few grand damask medallions at the maximum.

params.label: Symmetry
params.effect: Order of the dihedral kaleidoscope folding each motif; low gives a bold few-petalled rosette, high a finely spoked lace medallion.

params.label: Ornament
params.effect: Complexity of the foliate filigree; low is a clean simple motif, high crowds each medallion with intricate scrollwork.

params.label: Shimmer
params.effect: Speed of the gold shimmer travelling the filigree; 0 holds a still woven cloth, higher lets light roll slowly across the metal thread.

params.label: Sway
params.effect: A slow back-and-forth drift of the whole pattern so the brocade reads as a gently swaying drape; 0 pins it to a flat static print.

params.label: Morph
params.effect: How fast the foliate ornament evolves; 0 is a fixed motif, higher lets the filigree breathe and re-form while staying perfectly symmetric.

params.label: Rotation
params.effect: Turns the whole wallpaper to hang the medallion repeat on any angle.

params.label: Ground
params.effect: Richness of the deep jewel ground; low sinks it to near-black velvet, high lifts the cloth to a brighter dyed silk.

params.label: Gold
params.effect: Brightness of the gold filigree; low is a tarnished thread tone-on-tone with the ground, high a bright burnished metal that blooms.

params.label: Spacing
params.effect: Gap between the medallions without changing the grid; 0 is the packed repeat, higher shrinks each figure to open airy negative space, negative grows the figures so they OVERLAP their neighbours (the motifs interlace instead of cropping at the cell edge).
